existing_representation.x: cx_n uses an X-specific image-scale denominator W_i
existing_representation.y: cy_n uses a Y-specific image-scale denominator H_i
existing_representation.geometry_implication: When W_i != H_i, Euclidean distances/angles in (cx_n, cy_n) are anisotropically scaled relative to pixel geometry.

new_isotropic_branch.why_max_dimension: A single denominator preserves equal x/y metric scaling, preserves image aspect ratio, and keeps both coordinates within [0,1] without clipping.
new_isotropic_branch.velocity_rule: Recompute velocities/displacements from isotropic coordinates; do not reuse vx_n/vy_n.
new_isotropic_branch.canonicalization_rule: Recompute all translation/rotation/path-length canonicalization from isotropic coordinates.
new_isotropic_branch.frozen_branch_rule: Existing cx_n/cy_n datasets, checkpoints, predictions, conformal q, warning results and manuscript locks remain unchanged.

geometry_validation.velocity_rule: Do NOT rescale frozen vx_n/vy_n independently. Recompute velocity/displacement from cx_iso/cy_iso after transformation.
geometry_validation.canonicalization_rule: Any translation/rotation/path-length canonicalization in the R9 branch must be recomputed from isotropic coordinates; do not reuse anisotropic canonical tensors.
